glance_takeaway: This page is a post-incident infographic for incident INC-1194 at Ledgerline on 2026-06-24 — a 4h 17m partial outage that had no single root cause. Its main message is that three factors combined: a query regression from a 14:02 deploy (the trigger) plus two amplifiers — autovacuum debt (38.1M dead tuples from a Jun 22 backfill) and a retry storm with no jitter that saturated an 80-connection pgbouncer pool — and removing any one leg would have made it a minor one-endpoint slowdown rather than an outage. Impact was severe but contained: 31.2% peak error rate, 2,312 orgs (24.4%) affected, ~$41,300 in SLA credits, and zero records lost.

strengths: The causal structure (trigger + two amplifiers, remove-any-leg counterfactual) is the visual centerpiece and lands fully at a glance — exactly what the brief says matters most
Proportional SVG timeline is quantitatively honest (segment widths match 9/68/106/74 min) and directly answers 'why 4h17m'
Zero distortions or contradictions across 16 facts; every number on the page checks out against key_facts.md
DB concepts glossed for the non-specialist audience ('dead tuples - stale row copies awaiting cleanup'; pgbouncer pool = '80 database connections')
Dedicated caveat chip preserves measurement caveats and the blameless framing; accessible (aria-labels, dark-mode palette)
weaknesses: Only T1 of four takeaways is visible above the fold; the detection-lag, rollback, and remediation stories all live below the glance line
Three facts wholly absent: latency impact magnitudes (F3), the canary blind spot (F6), and the recovery mechanism (F14)
Poster-level compression leaves an EM under-armed to 'defend the P0 priorities in planning': no owners, no average error rate, no misdiagnosis anchors, no pool-bump-reverted subplot
Broken deploy markers — a load-bearing piece of the misdiagnosis story (T2) — are omitted from the detection caption
Depth is exhausted in about 90 seconds; a motivated 2-3 minute reader has nothing further to dig into
